problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{4}x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{4}x)
$$

Let $F(x)=-5x+2$ for $x\in [-4,4).$ The Fourier series of the $8$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${b}_{3}.$

${b}_{3}=$ {{field-1}}
worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the sine coefficients are given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{L}x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=4$ and $f(x)=-5x+2$ for $x\in [-4,4).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
{b}_{3}=\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{-4}^{4}(-5x+2)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=-5x+2\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=-5 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}x)\, & ⇒\,v=-\frac{4}{3\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}x)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{3} & =\frac{1}{4}(uv\,{|}_{-4}^{4}-{\int }_{-4}^{4}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(-\frac{4}{3\pi }{[(-5x+2)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}x)]}_{-4}^{4}-{\int }_{-4}^{4}(-\frac{4}{3\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}x))(-5)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(-\frac{4}{3\pi }{[(-5x+2)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}x)]}_{-4}^{4}-\frac{20}{3\pi }{\int }_{-4}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}x)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(-\frac{4}{3\pi }((-18)(-1)-(22)(-1))-\frac{80}{9{\pi }^{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-3\pi ))) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(-\frac{4}{3\pi }\cdot 40) \\  & =-\frac{40}{3\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$
